_meta.indication: AUSTEDO is a VMAT2 inhibitor indicated for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2-arm parallel-group, multi-center trial; patients randomized 1:1 to placebo and SD-809 (deutetrabenazine)
pivotal_trials.population: Ambulatory adult patients with manifest chorea associated with Huntington's disease (TMC score >= 8 required for inclusion)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: change from Baseline to maintenance therapy in Total Maximal Chorea (TMC) score
pivotal_trials.result: TMC score improved by LS mean -4.42 with AUSTEDO vs -1.93 with placebo; treatment difference -2.49 (95% CI -3.69, -1.29); p<0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>8% and greater than placebo) were somnolence, diarrhea, dry mouth, and fatigue; somnolence 11% vs 4% placebo, diarrhea 9% vs 0%, dry mouth 9% vs 7%, fatigue 9% vs 4%
target_moa: Vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitor; effect on chorea is believed to relate to reversible depletion of monoamines (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, histamine) from nerve terminals
modality: Small molecule (a selectively deuterated form of tetrabenazine)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: DEPRESSION AND SUICIDALITY — AUSTEDO can increase the risk of depression and suicidal thoughts and behavior in patients with Huntington's disease; balance risks against clinical need for treatment of chorea and monitor patients

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues

description.text: Added pediatric use labeling (section 8.4) for patients age 6 to 16 with Tourette Syndrome based on Written Request studies

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for labeling changes to section 8.4 (Pediatric Use), obtained from studies completed in response to our Written Request issued January 8, 2020, regarding the use of deutetrabenazine in patients age 6 to 16 for the treatment of Tourette Syndrome. These changes include description of studies conducted, relevant safety information, and description of juvenile animal toxicity data.

orphan_indication.text: Deutetrabenazine has orphan drug designation for Huntington's disease (an orphan disease); the product has orphan exclusivity

citations.quote: Deutetrabenazine has not been approved in any country, and has orphan drug designation.
As the product has orphan exclusivity, PREA was not triggered by this application.

summary.text: Deutetrabenazine (Austedo) was approved via the 505(b)(2) pathway using tetrabenazine (Xenazine) as the reference listed drug for treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease; it holds orphan drug designation, and approval followed a prior Complete Response letter of May 27, 2016 regarding characterization of major human metabolites

citations.quote: The 505(b)(2) application under review is for deutetrabenazine (Austedo), a deuterated form of tetrabenazine, proposed for the treatment of chorea associated with Huntington's disease. The applicant proposes using tetrabenazine, which is approved for the same indication, as reference listed drug.
Deutetrabenazine has not been approved in any country, and has orphan drug designation.
The submission under review is a response to a Complete Response letter that was issued on May 27, 2016.

basis.text: Clinical pharmacology studies were not adequate to determine whether all major human metabolites of deutetrabenazine have been identified (needed to support the bridge to the reference listed drug)
